Assume the Axiom of Choice and Countable Choice as declared by the cited weak-solvability and trace suppliers ([[def-axiom-of-choice]], [[def-countable-choice]]). Let $\Omega_v\subset\mathbb R^3$ be a bounded $C^\infty$ domain with finitely many connected components (the vacuum region of a conductor configuration by [[lem-em-vacuum-region-of-conductors-is-a-bounded-smooth-domain]], or any bounded smooth domain), let $\rho$ be continuous on $\overline{\Omega_v}$ (the fixed-time volume source density, C m$^{-3}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]), and let $\varphi_1,\varphi_2\in C^2(\overline{\Omega_v})$ be real potentials of the pure electrostatic regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with fields $E_i:=-\nabla\varphi_i$ of [[def-em-fields]] and
$$-\Delta\varphi_i=\rho/\varepsilon_0\qquad\text{pointwise on }\Omega_v,\qquad \Delta=\operatorname{div}\nabla\text{ of }\text{[[def-laplacian-of-a-c2-function]]}.$$
Let $\nu$ denote the outward unit normal of $\Omega_v$ ([[def-classical-normal-derivative]]). Then:
(a) [Classical Dirichlet uniqueness] if $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$ on $\partial\Omega_v$, then $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$ on $\overline{\Omega_v}$, and hence $E_1=E_2$. The conclusion holds component by component; each connected component of a bounded $C^\infty$ domain is again a bounded $C^\infty$ domain, to which the connected-domain uniqueness corollary applies.
(b) [Classical Neumann uniqueness and compatibility] if $\partial_\nu\varphi_1=\partial_\nu\varphi_2$ on $\partial\Omega_v$, then $\varphi_1-\varphi_2$ is constant on each connected component of $\Omega_v$, and conversely adding one real constant per component to a solution preserves both the equation and the Neumann data; hence the field $E$ is unique while the potential is determined only up to componentwise constants. Moreover the Neumann data are necessarily compatible:
$$\int_{\Omega_v^{(j)}}\rho\,dx+\varepsilon_0\int_{\partial\Omega_v^{(j)}}\partial_\nu\varphi\,dS=0\qquad\text{for every connected component }\Omega_v^{(j)}.$$
This compatibility is necessary, not sufficient, and is exactly the flux identity of the divergence theorem for the Poisson equation.
(c) [Weak variants] (i) if $g\in H^{1/2}(\partial\Omega_v)$ ([[def-fractional-sobolev-space-on-a-compact-c-one-boundary]]) is prescribed as a trace and $\varphi_1,\varphi_2\in H^1(\Omega_v)$ are weak solutions of the Dirichlet problem with the same trace $g$, then $\varphi_1=\varphi_2$; (ii) if the conormal data are prescribed compatibly, weak $H^1$ solutions are unique modulo constants on each connected component, and for connected $\Omega_v$ this is the normalised solution of [[lem-em-weak-neumann-and-transmission-existence]]; (iii) [sheet/transmission variant] for the finite disjoint smooth interfaces and outer Dirichlet data of [[thm-em-elliptic-boundary-existence]](c), the globally $H^1$ solution is unique, and for compatible outer Neumann data it is unique modulo componentwise constants until the componentwise means are fixed.
(d) [Physics reading and conductor case] for a pure electrostatic solution with $\operatorname{curl}E_i=0$ on a star-shaped vacuum domain, a potential with $E_i=-\nabla\varphi_i$ exists by [[pthm-em-electrostatic-potential]], so the hypotheses of (a)-(c) are met automatically; in the conductor model with prescribed component potentials $V_j$ and prescribed ambient data on $\partial\Omega$ the vacuum field is unique and the potential is unique up to the one constant fixed by the ambient/grounding data. In particular the potential is unique up to a global constant when at least one grounded boundary is specified, while with only conductor body data and no ground the constant is free.
(e) [Scope] uniqueness is conditional on the stated boundary or decay data: on an unbounded exterior region without a decay condition uniqueness fails: on $\Omega_R=\{x:|x|>R\}$ the functions $0$ and $u(x)=1-R/|x|$ are two distinct bounded harmonic functions with the same zero boundary trace and different limits at infinity (the witness is verified in the strategy), so the boundary, decay and regularity hypotheses above cannot be dropped. No existence is inferred from uniqueness; the classical branch requires $C^2$ up to the closure, the weak branches carry their own domain, coefficient and trace hypotheses, and no dielectric material coefficient or empirical claim is included.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ($\mathrm{AC}_\omega$) as carried by the integral and distribution interfaces ([[def-countable-choice]]). **Declare the ideal parallel-plate model** of two infinite parallel charged planes in vacuo, read as equipotential ideal conductor surfaces of the same equilibrium structure as [[post-em-electrostatic-conductor-model]] (the pure electrostatic regime [[def-em-electrostatic-regime]] with fields [[def-em-fields]]): for a separation parameter $d>0$, half-separation $h=d/2$, a surface-density parameter $\sigma>0$ (C m$^{-2}$) and the framework constants of [[def-em-si-conventions]], the model consists of the field
$$E(x):=\begin{cases}-\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}e_3,&|x_3|<h,\\[2pt]0,&|x_3|>h,\end{cases}\qquad x=(x_1,x_2,x_3),$$
together with the plane densities $+\sigma$ on $\Pi_+:=\{x_3=h\}$ and $-\sigma$ on $\Pi_-:=\{x_3=-h\}$, and with the piecewise potential $\varphi(x):=-\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}x_3$ for $|x_3|\le h$, $\varphi:=-\dfrac{\sigma h}{\varepsilon_0}$ for $x_3\ge h$ and $\varphi:=+\dfrac{\sigma h}{\varepsilon_0}$ for $x_3\le-h$. Then:
(a) [Direct distributional verification] $E$ and $\varphi$ are locally integrable and $C^\infty$ off $\Pi_+\cup\Pi_-$ with $E=-\nabla\varphi$ there, $\varphi$ is continuous on $\mathbb R^3$ and constant on each plane with the values $\varphi|_{\Pi_+}=-\sigma h/\varepsilon_0$, $\varphi|_{\Pi_-}=+\sigma h/\varepsilon_0$; and in $\mathcal D'(\mathbb R^3)$
$$\operatorname{div}E=\frac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\bigl(\delta_{\Pi_+}-\delta_{\Pi_-}\bigr),\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=0,$$
where $\delta_{\Pi_\pm}(\psi):=\int_{\mathbb R^2}\psi(x_1,x_2,\pm h)\,dx_1\,dx_2$ for compactly supported smooth $\psi$ are the plane distributions defined by the iterated Lebesgue integrals. Equivalently, the model realises the static electrostatic equations with the declared pair of plane densities and no other source, and the potential differences read off $\varphi$ are $\varphi(-h)-\varphi(h)=2\sigma h/\varepsilon_0=\sigma d/\varepsilon_0$.
(b) [Uniform field and voltage] the field between the planes has constant magnitude $|E|=\sigma/\varepsilon_0$ and is normal to the planes, and the potential difference between the plates is $V:=\varphi|_{\Pi_-}-\varphi|_{\Pi_+}=\sigma d/\varepsilon_0$.
(c) [Charge, capacitance and energy of the ideal model] for any chosen finite area $A>0$ the charge on the portion of area $A$ of the positive plate is $Q:=\sigma A$, so $Q=(\varepsilon_0A/d)V$ with the  ratio
$$C:=\frac QV=\frac{\varepsilon_0A}{d}>0,$$
independent of $\sigma$ and $V$; and the field energy contained in the slab of area $A$ between the plates is
$$U=\frac{\varepsilon_0}{2}\int_{\text{slab of area }A}|E|^2\,d\lambda_3=\frac{\sigma^2Ad}{2\varepsilon_0}=\frac12QV=\frac{Q^2}{2C}=\frac12CV^2 .$$
(d) [Relation to the bounded-conductor theorem and scope] the linearity $Q=CV$, the positivity $C>0$ and the energy identities $U=\frac12QV=\frac{Q^2}{2C}=\frac12CV^2$ are exactly the conclusions that [[pthm-em-capacitance-energy]] proves for bounded conductor configurations with prescribed potentials and a grounded reference; this example verifies them directly for the ideal model because the infinite planes and the unbounded declared field are outside that theorem's hypotheses (compact conductors in a bounded vacuum region) and outside the declared stationary-sheet source type of [[def-em-weak-sources]], exactly as the ideal line source lies outside the compact-source types of the electrostatic page. No approximation theorem from finite plates to the infinite model is asserted; for a finite real plate pair the uniform-field model neglects the fringing field near the edges, which is not computed here, and the idealisation also omits the finite-thickness, material, transient and measurement content of any real capacitor.

deltas.before: All identities are computed directly from the explicit piecewise formulas; no compact-sheet jump theorem is invoked, because the planes are noncompact and the model is a declared idealization. (a) Local integrability is immediate from the boundedness of the piecewise field and the finiteness of the slab's intersections with compact sets ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]], [[cor-continuous-functions-are-borel-measurable]]); the identification with regular distributions is [[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]] and [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]. For a compactly supported smooth test $\psi\in\mathcal D(\mathbb R^3)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]), $\langle\operatorname{div}E,\psi\rangle=-\int E\cdot\nabla\psi=-\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}\int_{|x_3|<h}\partial_3\psi\,d\lambda_3$ (inner product [[def-euclidean-inner-product]] and norm of [[lem-every-norm-on-rn-is-continuous-for-the-euclidean-metric]]); Fubini ([[thm-fubini-theorem-for-l-one-on-sigma-finite-product-spaces]]) writes the slab integral as $\int_{\mathbb R^2}\bigl(\int_{-h}^{h}\partial_3\psi(x_1,x_2,s)\,ds\bigr)dx_1dx_2$, and the inner integral is $\psi(x_1,x_2,h)-\psi(x_1,x_2,-h)$ by [[thm-integration-by-parts]] (the one-dimensional Newton-Leibniz identity, applicable because $\psi$ is smooth and compactly supported and the interval is bounded); hence $\langle\operatorname{div}E,\psi\rangle=\dfrac{\sigma}{\varepsilon_0}(\delta_{\Pi_+}-\delta_{\Pi_-})(\psi)$, proving the divergence identity with the sign convention of [[def-distributional-derivative]] and [[def-distribution]]. (b) is the explicit evaluation, and (c) is arithmetic with the slab integral computed by Fubini: $\int_{\text{slab}}|E|^2=\frac{\sigma^2}{\varepsilon_0^2}Ad$. (d) states the exact relation to [[pthm-em-capacitance-energy]]: that theorem's structure (linearity in the voltage, positive capacitance, energy equal to half the pairing $QV$) is what the computation reproduces, but its hypotheses (bounded conductor bodies, bounded vacuum region, Dirichlet solvability) are not met by the infinite-plane idealization, so the identities are verified here directly and the theorem is not applied; the fringing qualification is the design X2 warning, recorded as scope rather than computed.
